• A non-mechanical material which is able to join 2 substrates together using adhesive and cohesive mechanisms
• A material composed of polymers, in a liquid state when applied, that become solid during the curing process
• The materials that are to be bonded together
• A substances ability to stick to substrates (Bond strength)
• Adhesive forces are located in a thin layer (bond line) between the substrate and the adhesive itself
• When you pull apart a bond and the glue comes away from the substrate, this is adhesive failure
• A substances ability to stick to itself (Internal / tear strength)
• When you pull apart a bond and the adhesive itself splits, this is cohesive failure
• For an adhesive to work effectively, both adhesion and cohesion properties must be good
How does an adhesive bond to the substrate?
• There are many forms of adhesion, however the most common form is “Mechanical Bonding”
• Most substrates are porous (some more than others). A bond is formed when the adhesive works its way into the small pores of the substrate surface.
• This process acts like millions of microscopic screws and bolts being driven into both substrate surfaces to hold them together
• Weaker adhesives harden by some physical change, such as the evaporation of a solvent during cure
• Stronger adhesives solidify during a chemical change, such as the absorption of atmospheric moisture during cure
• Smooth substrate surfaces generally mean that pores or adhesion sites are smaller and less in number
• Rough substrate surfaces generally mean that pores or adhesion sites are larger and greater in number
• Stronger and more viscous adhesives will generally deliver sufficient bond strength on porous materials
• Weaker and/or less viscous adhesives are required to bond non-porous substrates
Less is more – do not use too much adhesive, it will not produce a better bond. In fact, too much adhesive will slow or even stop the curing process, leading to reduced performance
• During cold days there is less humidity in the atmosphere, therefore moisture cure adhesives will take longer to cure
• During warm days there is more humidity in the atmosphere, therefore moisture cure adhesives will cure faster
• Adhesives that are suitable for use on damp substrates will take longer to cure than when applied onto dry substrates
• Bonding non-porous materials together will slow the rate of adhesive cure, as there is limited adhesive area for solvents / water to evaporate or for moisture to be absorbed
• Do not store adhesives at very cold temperatures, this will make the products much more viscous and difficult to use

• Do not leave adhesives in the car or near heat sources prior to use, this will make the products very runny and difficult to control. Also, when opening tubes and cartridges, adhesives may squirt out under pressure when hot.
• Do not buy more adhesive than you think you will need for the job. Old, stored adhesives will not perform as well as fresh adhesives
• Use Sika re-sealable cartridge nozzles to keep your adhesive fresh during project down time and between jobs

What is concrete repair and protection, and when is it needed?

Concrete repair and protection involve restoring damaged concrete and addressing the causes of deterioration to help maintain a structure’s integrity, durability and appearance. Concrete repair may be required where concrete has been affected by reinforcement corrosion, water infiltration, chemical exposure, shrinkage, abrasion, physical damage or other deterioration.

Concrete protection helps reduce further deterioration by protecting reinforcement and concrete from factors such as water and dissolved contaminants. Sika Australia offers concrete repair solutions including repair mortars, corrosion protection systems, bonding primers, smoothing mortars and pore sealers, selected according to the condition and requirements of the structure.
How do I choose the right repair mortar for a structural repair project?

Choosing the right repair mortar starts with identifying the cause and extent of the concrete damage, along with the repair requirements of the structure. For structural repair, consider whether the concrete has deteriorated due to reinforcement corrosion, water infiltration, physical damage, chemical exposure or other underlying causes. The repair material should be suitable for the substrate and the specific repair application.

Sika repair mortars include cement-based, cementitious, polymer-modified and epoxy-based materials for different concrete repair requirements. Where reinforcement is exposed, appropriate corrosion protection and bonding preparation may also be required before applying the repair mortar.
What is the difference between repair mortar and smoothing mortar?

Repair mortar is used to restore damaged concrete and, where required, structural integrity, while smoothing mortar is intended for minor surface defects. Repair mortars can address defective, spalled or damaged concrete and help restore the original profile, function and durability of the concrete.

By comparison, smoothing mortars and pore fillers are used for issues such as surface pores and honeycombed concrete. They help improve the durability, aesthetic and geometric appearance of the surface and can provide a suitable surface for overcoating. The appropriate choice within Sika repair products depends on the extent and type of concrete defect and the required repair outcome.
Are Sika concrete repair systems suitable for bridge repair work?

Yes, Sika concrete repair systems are suitable for bridge repair work. Sika Australia’s concrete repair mortars are designed for restoration, repair of spalling and damaged concrete across different structures, including bridges, infrastructure and super-structures. They can help repair concrete defects and restore structural integrity and durability.

For bridge concrete repair, the appropriate repair strategy depends on the cause and extent of deterioration. Factors such as reinforcement corrosion, water infiltration, physical damage and chemical degradation should be assessed when selecting the repair system. Where reinforcement is exposed, corrosion protection and bonding preparation may also form part of the repair approach.
What products are recommended for tunnel concrete repair?

For tunnel concrete repair, the appropriate products depend on the type and extent of concrete deterioration and the required repair outcome. Sika repair mortars include cement-based, cementitious and polymer-modified materials, as well as epoxy-based repair materials, providing options for different concrete repair requirements.

For tunnel repair, the cause of deterioration should first be identified. Damage may result from corrosion, water infiltration, chemical exposure, physical damage or other underlying factors. Where reinforcement is exposed, corrosion protection and bonding primers may be required before applying a repair mortar. Sika Australia also offers smoothing mortars and pore fillers for minor surface defects.
Can concrete repair and protection systems be used on building façades?

Yes, Sika concrete repair systems can be used for building façade repair, where the repair requirements are appropriate. Sika Australia’s concrete repair mortars are designed to repair damaged and spalled concrete, restore structural integrity and durability, and improve the appearance of concrete structures.

For façade concrete repair, the cause of deterioration should be identified before selecting the repair approach. Potential causes include reinforcement corrosion, water infiltration, physical damage and chemical degradation. Smoothing mortars and pore fillers may also be suitable for minor surface defects such as pores and honeycombing, helping restore the façade’s aesthetic and geometric appearance.
How do you protect reinforced concrete from corrosion?

Protecting reinforced concrete from corrosion starts with identifying the cause of reinforcement deterioration and selecting an appropriate repair and protection strategy. Sika Australia recommends corrosion protection and bonding primers where required to bond repair mortars to existing cementitious or steel substrates, particularly where reinforcement has low concrete cover or chlorides are present. Exposed reinforcement should be properly prepared and protected with an anti-corrosion slurry.

As part of concrete repair, suitable Sika concrete repair products can help protect reinforcement and restore damaged concrete. Protection systems can also help prevent the ingress of water-dissolved contaminants and provide anti-carbonation or chemical resistance protection.
What's the difference between epoxy adhesive and cement-based glue adhesive for concrete repair?

The main difference is the material type and the repair application each is intended to address. An epoxy adhesive is one of the epoxy-based repair materials available for specific concrete repair requirements, while cement-based materials include pure cement-based and cementitious repair products.

For structural bonding, the suitable material depends on the substrate, repair requirements and condition of the concrete. Sika Australia provides different repair materials for specific applications rather than treating one adhesive type as suitable for every repair. Corrosion protection and bonding primers may also be used to bond repair mortars to existing cementitious or steel substrates where required.
Can a self-levelling concrete floor product be used to repair uneven or damaged floors?
Yes, a self levelling concrete floor product can be used to repair uneven concrete floors in many situations. Sika Australia offers Sikafloor Level TOP,

a high-flowing self levelling concrete underlayment designed to level uneven concrete substrates before floor coverings are installed. It can be laid from 1 mm to 30 mm in a single application, making it suitable for concrete floor repair where the substrate requires smoothing.
For uneven concrete floor conditions, the product must be compatible with the substrate and the intended floor finish. Sikafloor Level Ultra

is a fibre-reinforced option that can be applied from 1 mm to 50 mm and is suitable for interior and exterior concrete substrates. Substrate preparation and priming remain essential before application.
How can cracks in concrete be repaired to stop water getting in?
Repairing waterproofing cracks in concrete requires identifying the cause and selecting an appropriate injection system. Sika Australia offers injection resin solutions including Sika Injection-306

, a polyacrylic elastic resin for permanent watertight sealing of water-bearing cracks. Sika Injection-111 is a hydrophobic semi-flexible polyurethane grout designed to stop active water flow in cracks and joints.
For cracks where movement is a factor, Sika Injection-222

is a hydrophilic flexible polyurethane grout that reacts with water to form a permanently flexible seal. A flexible sealant may also be considered for certain joint applications, but the appropriate system depends on crack width, water pressure and whether structural bonding is required.

Sika develops and markets a complete range of admixtures and additives for use in concrete, cement and mortar production. These products enhance specific properties of the fresh and hardened concrete, such as workability, watertightness, durability, or early and final strength.

The demand for admixtures and additives is currently on the rise, particularly due to the increased performance requirements placed on concrete and mortar, especially in urban areas and for infrastructure construction. Furthermore, the growing use of alternative materials such as manufactu­red sands, alternative binders and supplementary materials in mortar and concrete, is increasing the need for admixtures.

Extended workability, controlled over several hours, is especially important for urban construction sites with congested traffic, or remote areas resulting in long transportation times. At the same time, once the concrete is placed, fast curing is of utmost importance to meet tight construction schedules. Sika ViscoFlow is workability enhancing admixture, based on a new in-house-developed polymer which significantly prolongs the workability time of the fresh concrete and still ensures equally fast strength development. The workability time can be modified in accordance with job site requirements.

Concrete, the single most widely-used building material in the world, has a history dating back to the Romans and ancient Egyptians. Given that concrete is used twice as much in construction over all other building materials, emphasis on quality, performance and sustainability is essential for the industry to grow and thrive.

One of the most important ingredients in high performance, long-lasting, durable and beautiful concrete produced today are concrete admixtures. Concrete admixtures are natural or manufactured chemicals or additives added during concrete mixing to enhance specific properties of the fresh or hardened concrete, such as workability, durability, or early and final strength.

Just like us, concrete needs to be maintained. It is affected by the stresses and strains of everyday life.

Deterioration of concrete may happen due to corrosion, structural damage, water infiltration, seismic activity or a multitude of other reasons. Years of research plus decades of practical experience have enabled Sika to develop a fully comprehensive solution to restore and rehabilitate concrete structures. Sika customer advice and support is second to none, from concept to successful completion on site. This is all based on more than 100 years of experience on large and small projects all over the world.

Sika is the leading company for fibre-reinforced concrete solutions. Our global footprint and a fibre production facility in all regions means we are ideally placed to support your project.

Local technical support is valuable to our customers. As a multi-discipline construction materials company, Sika offers a full range of solutions for concrete including admixtures, curing agents, mold release agents, floor hardening and coatings, joint sealants, concrete protection and more. What are concrete fibres and why are they added to concrete?

Concrete fibres are small reinforcing fibres added to concrete or mortar to improve durability and toughness. In fibre reinforced concrete, they can help reduce shrinkage cracking, increase strength and energy absorption, and reduce dangerous spalling when concrete is exposed to high temperatures.

The type and performance of concrete fibre reinforcement depend on the fibre selected and the intended application. Sika Australia supplies a range of fibre solutions, including polyolefin macro-synthetic, blended synthetic, polypropylene and steel fibres for reinforced concrete and shotcrete. The appropriate fibre should be selected according to the project requirements and concrete application.
What's the difference between steel and synthetic fibres for concrete?

Steel fiber reinforcement and synthetic fibres provide different reinforcement options for concrete. Sika Australia offers collated hooked-end steel fibres as well as polyolefin macro-synthetic and polypropylene fiber products. These are designed for different concrete and shotcrete applications, so selection should be based on the required reinforcement performance and project conditions.

as a steel fibre option. Synthetic options include macro, micro and blended fibres. Are steel fibres suitable for concrete floors and pavements?

Yes, steel fibers for concrete are suitable for concrete floors and pavements, providing uniform multi-directional reinforcement that improves crack resistance, ductility and load-carrying capacity. Sika Australia supplies steel fibre reinforced concrete solutions for ground-supported slabs, external roads and pavements, with products designed for industrial and heavy-duty applications.

Steel fibre reinforced concrete is typically dosed according to the application and required performance. The fibres bridge cracks and improve impact resistance, making them suitable for industrial floors and heavy-duty pavements where conventional mesh reinforcement may be impractical. The appropriate fibre type and dosage should be confirmed against the specific product documentation.
How are fibres added to a concrete mix on site?

Fibres are added directly to the concrete mix during batching or mixing, with the specific addition method depending on the fibre product and concrete application. The selected fibre for concrete mix should be incorporated according to the manufacturer’s technical instructions to achieve the intended distribution throughout the concrete.

Sika Australia offers a range of fibre reinforcement solutions, including macro-synthetic, micro-synthetic, blended and steel fibres for concrete and shotcrete. Can concrete fibres be used in screeds?

For a screed application, the appropriate fibre should be selected according to the screed formulation and project requirements. Sika Australia provides several synthetic and steel fibre options. Product-specific documentation should be checked before use to confirm compatibility with the specific screed mix and application. Are concrete fibres used in precast concrete elements?

Yes, concrete fibres are used in precast concrete elements. Sika Australia supplies both synthetic and steel fibre options for precast applications. Synthetic fibres such as Sika Fibre help reduce plastic shrinkage cracking, while macro-synthetic and steel fibres can enhance toughness and load-carrying capacity.

The appropriate concrete fibre reinforcement depends on the element's structural requirements, manufacturing process and exposure conditions. Sika Australia provides technical support to help select suitable fibre reinforcement solutions for precast concrete projects, ensuring the correct fibre is used for each specific application.
What are macro synthetic fibres used for in concrete?

Macro synthetic fibres are used in concrete to improve its durability and toughness performance. They can help reduce shrinkage cracking, increase strength and energy absorption, and reduce dangerous spalling when concrete is exposed to high temperatures.
Macro synthetic fibre reinforced concrete can incorporate products such as SikaFiber Force PP-48/RAD-48s

Do polypropylene fibres help prevent cracking in concrete?

Yes. Polypropylene fibres for concrete can help reduce shrinkage cracking. Sika Australia states that fibres in concrete help reduce shrinkage cracks while also improving durability and toughness performance. Its fibre range includes Sika Confibre 19F
and Sika Confibre 51F, which are fibrillated polypropylene fibres, as well as Sika Fibermesh-150, a micro-synthetic monofilament fibre.

The suitable fibre type depends on the concrete application and required performance. Sika Australia also offers technical support to help select an appropriate fibre solution for specific concrete projects.
What is a cement fibre additive and how is the dosage determined?

A cement fibre additive is a fibre reinforcement added to concrete or mortar to improve properties such as toughness and durability. Sika Australia’s fibre solutions include synthetic, polyolefin, polypropylene and steel fibres, with applications depending on the product and concrete requirements.

The dosage is not a single standard amount and should be determined according to the selected fibre, concrete mix, application and required performance. Sika Australia provides a fibre selection chart and technical support to help identify an appropriate solution. Product-specific documentation should be followed when determining the required dosage rather than applying a generic fibre rate.

What is a cement levelling system and when is it used before flooring installation?
A cement levelling system is a cement-based underlayment used to correct uneven or irregular substrates and create a flat, smooth and consistent surface ready for the installation of floor coverings.

It is commonly used over new or existing concrete where there are variations in floor level, rough surfaces or imperfections that could affect the appearance and performance of the finished floor. Cement levelling compounds can be applied in different thicknesses depending on the condition of the substrate and project requirements.

Sika Australia offers a range of Sikafloor cement levelling systems for commercial and residential applications, including solutions suitable for small areas through to large-scale floor levelling projects.
Correct substrate preparation, product selection and installation are important to provide a stable, level and suitable surface for the final floor covering.
Which self-levelling compound should I use for an uneven concrete floor?

The right self-levelling compound depends on the condition of the concrete, required build-up thickness, installation environment and the final floor covering. Sika Australia offers several Sikafloor levelling solutions for different project requirements.

The substrate should always be assessed for surface condition, porosity, required levelling depth and final floor covering before selecting the levelling compound and primer.
How is a self-levelling cement compound applied to a concrete substrate?
A self-levelling cement compound is applied over a sound, clean and properly prepared concrete substrate to create a smooth, level surface ready for the final floor covering.

The concrete is first prepared to remove dust, laitance, contamination and loose material. A compatible Sikafloor primer is then applied before the levelling compound is mixed with clean water and poured or pumped onto the floor. The material is spread to the required thickness and allowed to flow and level across the surface. Sika Australia offers compatible primers, moisture barriers and levelling compounds as part of its subfloor preparation range.

Once sufficiently dry, the levelled surface provides a smooth and consistent base for the selected floor covering. Product-specific requirements for preparation, priming, application thickness and drying time should always be followed.
Can cement levelling compounds be used before installing tiles, vinyl or timber flooring?

Cement levelling compounds are commonly used to create a smooth, level and consistent substrate before installing tiles, vinyl, timber and other floor coverings. Sika Australia offers a range of Sikafloor levelling systems designed as underlayments for commercial and residential flooring applications.

What substrate preparation is required before applying a levelling compound?

Proper substrate preparation is essential to achieve a strong, smooth and durable levelling system. The substrate should be sound, clean and free from dust, loose material and contaminants that could affect adhesion.

Cracks, holes and damaged areas should be repaired as required, and the surface should be prepared to suit the condition and porosity of the substrate. A compatible Sikafloor primer should then be applied before the levelling compound to help control substrate porosity and improve adhesion.

What causes an uneven or cracked finish after applying a self-levelling compound?

What is epoxy flooring and how does it work on concrete surfaces?

Epoxy flooring is a resin-based flooring system applied over prepared concrete to create a seamless, hard-wearing and durable surface. Epoxy resin flooring works by bonding to a sound, mechanically prepared concrete substrate, forming a continuous coating or topping that protects the concrete. It is commonly used in industrial and commercial environments such as warehouses, workshops, manufacturing facilities, laboratories, food-related facilities and plant rooms requiring mechanical, chemical, hygienic or slip-resistant performance.

Sika Australia describes epoxy resin flooring as suitable for demanding industrial and commercial environments and offers systems ranging from floor coating concrete products to self-levelling, broadcast, decorative, ESD and resin flooring options.
Which epoxy flooring system is best suited for high-traffic commercial areas?

The best commercial epoxy flooring system for high-traffic areas depends on the operating environment and required floor performance. Factors include traffic type, mechanical loads, slip resistance and the desired surface finish. Commercial epoxy floor coating selection should therefore match each project’s specific performance requirements.
Sika Australia offers a range of systems, including Sikafloor MultiDur EB-24
, a multi-layer textured epoxy floor with high mechanical resistance, and Sikafloor MultiDur ES-24

, a high-build, self-levelling system for smooth or finely textured finishes. Epoxy floor coating suppliers and epoxy flooring installers should always confirm the selected system against traffic, cleaning and exposure conditions before installation.
Can epoxy flooring be installed directly over existing tiles?

Epoxy flooring is generally designed for application over sound, mechanically prepared concrete, cementitious substrates or epoxy mortar. For Sikafloor epoxy flooring systems, the substrate must be structurally sound and capable of providing adequate adhesion, typically with a minimum pull-off bond strength of 1.5 MPa (N/mm²). Sikafloor-160
, for example, is intended for priming concrete substrates, cement screeds and epoxy mortars and reports a tensile adhesion strength of 1.5 N/mm² with failure in the concrete.

Existing tiles should therefore not automatically be considered a suitable substrate for direct epoxy application. If tiles are to remain in place, the entire tiled assembly, including the tile, tile adhesive and underlying substrate, must be assessed to ensure it is sound, firmly bonded and capable of achieving the required bond strength after appropriate mechanical surface preparation.

Where the existing tiled surface cannot demonstrate the required ≥ 1.5 MPa pull-off strength, or where tiles are loose, hollow, cracked or inadequately bonded, the tiles should be removed and the underlying concrete prepared before installing the Sikafloor epoxy system.
Is epoxy flooring suitable for residential garages and homes?

Yes. Epoxy flooring can be suitable for residential garages and selected areas of the home, particularly where a seamless, hard-wearing and easy-to-maintain surface is required. Sika Australia’s Sikafloor epoxy range includes high-build, self-levelling, textured, non-slip and decorative flooring systems.

For residential garages, epoxy flooring can provide a durable surface suitable for vehicle traffic and general wear. Depending on the required appearance and slip resistance, the floor can be finished as a smooth coating, textured system or decorative finish.
Can epoxy flooring be used outdoors and in exposed, wet-weather areas?

Epoxy flooring can be used in some exposed areas, but not all epoxy systems are suitable for outdoor or wet-weather applications. System selection should consider UV exposure, weather conditions, substrate condition and required slip resistance.

Sika Australia offers textured and broadcast Sikafloor epoxy systems where increased slip resistance is required. Conventional epoxy flooring may also experience colour change when exposed to direct sunlight, so an appropriate protective topcoat may be required depending on the selected system and exposure conditions. Always refer to the relevant Sikafloor system and product documentation to confirm suitability for the intended outdoor application.
How durable is epoxy flooring in industrial and warehouse environments?

Epoxy flooring is highly durable when the right system is installed over a properly prepared, sound substrate. Sika Australia’s Sikafloor epoxy systems are designed for demanding industrial and commercial environments, providing hard-wearing surfaces suitable for areas exposed to regular traffic, abrasion and mechanical wear.
For heavier-duty applications, systems such as Sikafloor MultiDur EB-24
provide a high-build, multi-layer textured epoxy floor with high mechanical resistance, making them suitable for more demanding service conditions.

The long-term durability of an epoxy floor depends on factors such as substrate condition and preparation, system type and thickness, traffic and mechanical loads, chemical exposure, and ongoing maintenance. Selecting the Sikafloor system to match the expected operating conditions is therefore essential for achieving reliable, long-lasting performance.
What substrate preparation is needed before applying an epoxy flooring system?

Proper substrate preparation is essential for the performance and durability of an epoxy floor. The concrete or cementitious substrate must be sound, clean and capable of achieving a minimum pull-off bond strength of 1.5 MPa.

The surface should be mechanically prepared, typically by diamond grinding or shot blasting, to remove laitance, weak material, existing coatings and contamination, and to provide a suitable surface profile for adhesion. Oil, grease, dust and other contaminants must be completely removed.

Cracks, holes and surface defects should be repaired, and uneven areas may require levelling before the epoxy system is applied. The substrate moisture content and site conditions must also comply with the requirements of the selected Sikafloor primer and flooring system. For example, Sikafloor-161 is specified for concrete, cement screeds and epoxy mortars and can accommodate elevated substrate moisture content below 6% by weight.
Correct surface preparation is critical to achieving a strong, durable bond between the Sikafloor epoxy flooring system and the substrate.
What colour and finish options are available for epoxy flooring?

Sika Australia offers Sikafloor epoxy flooring in a broad range of colours and finishes to suit functional and decorative requirements. Standard colours are available from our product colour chart. Custom colours may be available subject to project requirements and minimum order quantities.
Finish options can include smooth gloss, self-levelling, textured and slip-resistant surfaces, as well as decorative vinyl flake systems. Sikafloor-264
provides a gloss finish with the option of a slip-resistant surface, while Sikafloor-264 T AU
provides a durable textured, non-slip finish.
The appropriate colour and finish should be selected based on the required appearance, traffic conditions, cleaning requirements and slip resistance.
Why might an epoxy floor coating fail to bond properly to a concrete substrate?

A concrete epoxy floor coating may fail to bond when concrete is weak, contaminated, inadequately prepared or excessively moist. Common causes include insufficient mechanical preparation leaving laitance; oil, grease, dust, curing compounds or contaminants; unsound concrete lacking pull-off strength; excessive substrate moisture outside primer limits; and condensation during application.

, substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3°C above dew point. Incorrect primer, mixing or application can also cause failure. For reliable adhesion, epoxy floor coatings for concrete, cement epoxy floor and concrete epoxy floor systems require a sound, clean, mechanically prepared substrate within specified moisture limits and capable of required bond strength.
How much does epoxy flooring typically cost compared to other flooring systems?

Epoxy flooring cost depends on the specific system, substrate condition, surface preparation, floor area, required thickness, finish and performance requirements. For commercial and industrial projects, compare the overall flooring solution rather than epoxy flooring price alone.

Epoxy floor coating systems can provide a seamless, hard-wearing and long-lasting surface suited to demanding environments. When comparing epoxy with other resin flooring, consider durability, maintenance, expected traffic, chemical and mechanical exposure, slip resistance and service life as part of overall value. Sikafloor epoxy systems are selected and specified according to project service conditions and required performance; a project-specific assessment is recommended to determine the most appropriate and cost-effective solution.

A bridge deck needs to be decoupled from the connecting road and columns to allow for thermal expansion and contraction, seismic movement, dynamic loads and other movements of the bridge. This is done by constructing a bridge deck expansion joint.

Such joints often must also prevent de-icing chemicals or other corrosives from penetrating into the substructure. They are highly exposed and are one of the first components that can fail on a bridge, possibly leading to dangerous traffic accidents and long traffic jams. Thus, an early and fast repair for expansion joints is critical for an improved urban area experience.
Using Sika FastFix-138 TT for bridge deck expansion joint repair allows for a fast return to service (within a few hours) and for easy application even at low temperatures.
To reduce high maintenance cost, implementation of a durable solution like the EMSEAL bridge expansion joint system (BEJS) is recommended for new construction.
Another Sika product, Sikasil-728 SL , is designed to seal saw cut and expansion joints in pavement not only on bridges, but also on highways, airports, garage driveways and car park top decks.

Are SikaRoofVersiPave and SikaRoofVersiJack pedestals systems adjustable?
Yes. SikaRoof pedestal systems are designed to create level raised surfaces across a wide range of paving and decking applications. SikaRoofVersiPave
features snap-on chocks that provide height adjustment from 24 mm to 34 mm, with additional adjustment available using extenders. SikaRoofVersiJack
offers a wider adjustment range from 37 mm to 1030 mm, making both systems suitable for a variety of project requirements.
Are SikaRoof pedestals systems strong and safe?

Yes. SikaRoof pedestal systems are engineered to provide stable support for raised paving and decking applications. By eliminating the need for traditional sand bedding, they can help reduce structural loading while creating level, secure surfaces. Their ability to accommodate uneven substrates also helps improve safety and usability in outdoor environments.
Do SikaRoof pedestals systems make installation and mainteance easier?

Yes. SikaRoof pedestal systems are designed for efficient installation and provide easy access to waterproofing membranes and concealed building services beneath the finished surface. This simplifies inspections, maintenance and future repairs while minimising disruption. The raised design also promotes drainage and ventilation beneath the surface, helping reduce water pooling and surface-related maintenance issues.

What is the difference between a construction sealant and a construction adhesive?

A construction sealant is primarily used to seal joints, gaps and movement areas against air, water or other environmental exposure, while an adhesive is intended mainly for bonding or securing materials together. Construction adhesive products are generally selected where the primary requirement is to bond substrates, whereas sealants are used where joint movement and weatherproofing are important.

Sika Australia offers dedicated product ranges for both sealing and bonding applications, including facade sealants, movement and construction joints, waterproofing sealants and construction adhesive systems. The appropriate product depends on the substrates, joint conditions and intended application.
Can sealants and adhesives be applied to concrete, timber and metal substrates?

Yes, Sika Australia offers sealants and adhesives for a range of construction materials and applications, including bonding and sealing work involving different substrates. However, suitability depends on the specific product, substrate and intended application. Products should be selected according to their technical documentation rather than using one adhesive across all materials.

For example, an adhesive for wood, metal adhesive glue or tile adhesive may have different performance and application requirements. A construction adhesive should only be used where the product information confirms compatibility with the substrate and conditions of the installation.
Are construction sealants suitable for use in wet areas like bathrooms and showers?

Construction sealants are suitable for wet areas such as bathrooms and showers, but the product must be specified for the intended application. Sika Australia offers sealant systems for applications including sanitary areas and waterproofing, so selection should be based on the product’s documented suitability rather than using a general purpose sealant.

A bathroom sealant, water resistant sealant or silicone sealant may be appropriate for certain joints, depending on the substrate and conditions. A waterproof sealant should not be assumed to replace a complete waterproofing system where one is required.
What surface preparation is required before applying a construction adhesive?

Construction adhesive should be applied only after the substrate is properly prepared. Surfaces should be clean, sound and free from dust, dirt, grease, loose material and other contaminants that could affect adhesion. Remove any adhesive residue remover contamination or residue where necessary, following the cleaner manufacturer's instructions.

The preparation method depends on the substrate and adhesive type. A contact adhesive may have different requirements from products used for general bonding and sealing, so always follow the relevant Sika Australia product instructions for cleaning, priming and application. Sika Australia provides dedicated cleaners, activators and primers for sealant and adhesive applications, which may form part of the required preparation.
Can construction adhesives be used to bond metal-to-metal surfaces?

Construction adhesives can be suitable for metal-to-metal bonding, but suitability depends on the specific adhesive, metals involved and service conditions. A metal adhesive glue or adhesive for metal should be selected only where the product documentation confirms compatibility with the substrates and intended application.

Sika Australia provides construction adhesives and contact adhesive products for different bonding applications. They should not be treated as interchangeable, as each product has specific performance characteristics. Sika Australia also offers cleaners, activators and primers for adhesive applications, which may form part of the required surface preparation. Follow the relevant product instructions for substrate preparation and application to achieve a reliable bond.
Why does silicone sealant fail or lose adhesion over time?

Silicone sealant can lose adhesion over time when the joint is poorly prepared, contaminated, or exposed to conditions outside the product’s intended application. Sika Australia guidance states that substrates should be clean, dry, sound and free from oil, grease, dust, cement laitance and loose material. Incorrect or uncontrolled priming can also affect performance.

Exposure to movement, moisture, incompatible materials or unsuitable substrates can also contribute to failure. When replacing failed silicone sealant, remove existing residue with an appropriate silicone sealant remover and prepare the surface again. The correct weather sealant or structural silicone should then be selected according to the substrate and application requirements.
What is the correct application method for fire-rated sealants in construction joints?

Fire-rated sealants should be applied according to the specific product system and the joint or penetration being protected. Sika Australia provides fire-rated solutions designed to seal penetrations and joints, helping restrict the spread of fire, smoke and heat for a specified period.

For a fire mastic or other construction sealants, the correct application method depends on the product and approved system. An expansion joint sealant should likewise be selected and installed for the relevant joint requirements. Do not assume a general sealant adhesive is suitable for fire protection. Follow the applicable Sika Australia product documentation and specified fire-rated system for installation details and requirements.

Here at Sika we understand that when it comes to safety on work sites and working with internal or external tiling projects, that there are plenty of things to consider. We know that any reduction in being exposed to silica dust can only be a positive choice to lessen the likelihood of exposure to harmful and often hard to detect with the human eye, silica dust.
Silica Free technology has been developed by our Sika technical department to create formulations that comply with AS ISO 13007 – Class C2TES1 without the use of any silica sand.

According to Safe Work Australia, the 8-hour time weighted average workplace exposure standard (WES) for respirable crystalline silica is recommended to be reduced from 0.1 mg/m3 to 0.02mg/m3 to minimise the risk of silicosis and lung cancer. Products containing silica sand may be below the limit but may still contain RCS. Sika formulates its products without silica sand , contributing to efforts to minimise silica dust exposure in construction environments..

What is the Davco tile adhesive range, and is a premixed option available?

The Davco tile adhesive range includes cement-based and pre-mixed paste adhesives designed for different tiles, substrates and installation conditions. Davco adhesives bond materials including ceramic, porcelain, mosaics, marble, natural stone, slate and granite across interior and exterior walls and floors.

Davco is a range of proven solutions for bonding tile and stone. Some pre-mixed options are perfectly suited for DIYers or professionals who benefit from ready-to-use convenience. Davco Grey One Pot adhesive

is a pre-mixed, ready-to-use flexible tile adhesive. Other Davco products include Powder Mastic, SMP EVO, Ultraflex, Ceramacrete, Ceramaflex and Supamastic, with selection depending on the specific tiling application.
How is grout injected or applied after tiles are laid with adhesive?

Grout is applied once the tiles are firmly fixed and the adhesive has cured for the time stated in the product data sheet. Clean the joints of dust and excess adhesive, mix the grout as instructed, then press it into the joints with a rubber grout float and remove the excess from the tile face. Clean off any haze with a damp sponge and allow the grout to cure. Grout injection is a different technique, used to fill voids rather than finish tile joints. When choosing from Sika's construction chemicals grout range, consider the tile type, joint width and exposure conditions.
Can the same adhesive be used for ceramic and mosaic tiles?

Yes, the same adhesive can suit both ceramic and mosaic tiles when it is specified for both tile types and the substrate and installation conditions. Sika Australia offers tile adhesives formulated for a wide range of materials, including ceramic and mosaic tiles. For example, SikaTile-400 EVO PRO

is a flexible cement-based adhesive designed for natural stone, porcelain and mosaics, while the broader range includes adhesives suitable for ceramic tiles. However, some glass mosaics may be opaque or translucent and require a white adhesive so the adhesive does not dull the mosaic’s appearance. Select ceramic tile adhesive or mosaic tile adhesive for the tile, substrate and application.
What type of tile adhesive works best for natural stone tiles?

A suitable stone tile adhesive should be selected based on the natural stone type, substrate and installation conditions. A white, flexible cement based adhesive is generally the best choice. White adhesive helps prevent discoloration or staining of light-coloured stone, while flexibility handles small movement and helps prevent cracking.

A rapid setting adhesive may be needed for moisture-sensitive stone. Sika Australia offers tile adhesives for natural stone, including marble, slate and granite, with different formulations. The range includes flexible cement-based and tile-and-stone adhesives, such as SikaTile-400 EVO PRO
for natural stone, porcelain and mosaics, and SikaTile-405 Lite
Is a flexible tile adhesive needed for shower walls?

Yes, because construction is typically completed over a frame background, a flexible tile adhesive should always be considered for shower wall tiling. Select a minimum S1 class adhesive for shower walls to accommodate small movements and reduce cracking or debonding. The adhesive should suit the tile, substrate and specific tiling conditions.

Sika Australia offers several flexible tile adhesive products, including flexible cement-based and polymer-fortified formulations. The range is designed for different tile types and substrates, including waterproofing membranes, plasterboard, fibre cement and concrete. Select the appropriate shower wall tile adhesive based on the complete shower tiling system and installation requirements.
What tile adhesive is suitable for wet areas like bathrooms?

For wet areas such as bathrooms, choose a tile adhesive for wet areas that can be subjected to water exposure, remains flexible and has a strong bond to various tile types, including porcelain. A C2TES1 class tile adhesive is considered appropriate for most applications. The bathroom tile adhesive must also suit the specific tiles, substrate and installation conditions, including waterproofing membranes, concrete, fibre cement and plasterboard.

Sika Australia offers cement-based and pre-mixed paste adhesives, including flexible cement-based and polymer-fortified options for ceramic, porcelain, natural stone and mosaics. Select the adhesive to be compatible with the complete tiling system and intended application.
Can tile adhesive be used for tiling a swimming pool?
Yes, tile adhesive can be used for swimming pool tiling when the product is specifically rated for submerged applications. Sika Australia offers SikaTile-510 Mega Lite
, a highly flexible, cement-based adhesive suitable for internal and external wall and floor applications, including pools and spas. Davco SMP EVO
is another flexible, cement-based option suitable for swimming pools and spas.

For pool joints and perimeter sealing, a sika swimming pool sealant such as Sikasil Pool is designed for permanently wet areas and offers resistance to chlorinated water. The adhesive and sealant must be compatible with the waterproofing system beneath the tiles, and the full tiling system should be specified together.
What's the difference between wall tile adhesive and floor tile adhesive?

The main difference between wall tile adhesive and floor tile adhesives is how they are designed to perform. Wall tile adhesive is designed to grip and hold tiles, preventing them from slipping down the wall during installation. Floor tile adhesive is designed to handle foot traffic, weight and movement while keeping tiles securely in place.

Selection depends on the tile, substrate, location and installation conditions, so the same product should not automatically be used for every application. Sika Australia offers tile adhesives for commercial and domestic walls and floors, including flexible cement-based, polymer-fortified and specialised options for porcelain, ceramic, natural stone and mosaics. Select the adhesive for the tiling application.
Which tile adhesive should I use for exterior tiling projects?

Choose a tile adhesive with improved bond strength and flexibility, that can accomodate water ingress from rain, thermal stresses/movement. Select an adhesive class C2TES1 as a minimum to accomodate the expected stresses. Sika Australia offers tile adhesives formulated for different installation requirements, including cement-based and flexible options.

The range can be used with tiles such as porcelain, ceramic, natural stone, slate and granite on substrates including concrete, brickwork, fibre cement, screed and waterproofing membranes. For specific exterior applications, the appropriate exterior tile adhesive should be selected based on the tile and substrate characteristics. SikaTile products include flexible cement-based options designed for particular tile types and installation requirements.

What is tile grout and what role does it play in a tiling installation?

Tile grout is the material used to fill the joints between tiles after installation, completing the tile and grout system. It helps keep dirt and moisture out of the gaps, supports the tile edges, and gives the tiled surface a neat, finished look. Grout for tiles is not waterproof, so wet areas still need proper waterproofing underneath. Sika Australia offers cement-based and epoxy-based options.

The appropriate tile grout "how to" approach depends on joint width, location and exposure. Cement-based grout comes in sanded and non-sanded forms; epoxy grout offers high water and chemical resistance. Grouting and sealing are separate steps, with sealers protecting tiles and grout from stains and soiling.
How do I choose the right grout colour for my tiling project?
Choosing the right tile grout colours depends on tile type, joint width and installation location.
For wall and floor tiles, choose grout for tiles suitable for the tile type and joint width.
In bathrooms and wet areas, use a water-resistant, mould-resistant grout.
For natural stone, choose a grout that will not stain or scratch the stone.

Coloured grout can match the tiles for a seamless look or provide contrast for a bold finish. Tile grout colourant products can refresh existing grout. Grout tiles colour selection should also consider cleaning and maintenance. Confirm the tile grout colours suit the tile, joint and exposure before grouting.
Is epoxy grout suitable for wet areas such as showers and bathrooms?

Epoxy grout is perfectly suited for showers and wet areas. Epoxy grout for shower applications is highly chemical resistant, almost stain resistant and virtually waterproof, making epoxy tile grout a suitable option for bathrooms. Shower grout must suit the tile system and joint requirements.
For bathroom installations, epoxy tile grout can be used where the specified product is suitable for the tile system and joint requirements. SikaCeram-880 Easy Epoxy

is an epoxy tile grout and adhesive. While epoxy grout offers high water resistance, it should not be described as a substitute for a complete waterproofing system. Select epoxy grout for shower and bathroom areas according to the tile, substrate and joint conditions, and confirm the product is suitable for the complete tiling system.
How is grout applied and sealed once tiles have been installed?

Once tiles are fixed and set, apply grout to fill the joints between the tiles. Mix the grout in accordance with the product data sheet. Apply the grout to joints with a grout float, ensuring joints are fully packed. Remove excess grout with a damp sponge before it dries. Allow the grout to cure as directed on the product data sheet. Then seal the grout with a penetrating sealer that reduces absorption and prevents stains and moisture.

Grouting and sealing require suitable tools for grouting and a compatible grout sealant. Sealing tile grout should follow sealer instructions. Confirm the grout for tiles type matches joint width and application before starting.
Can tile grout be used for both indoor and outdoor tiling applications?

Yes, tile grout can be used for both indoor and outdoor tiling applications. Floor tile grout and grouting floor tiles require products suited to the location, joint width and exposure. There are premium higher-performance options with improved performance characteristics that can be considered for demanding exterior conditions. Outdoor epoxy grout offers high water and chemical resistance, making it suitable where greater durability is required.

Tile grout floor applications should match the grout to the tile, substrate and weather exposure. For exterior work, select outdoor epoxy grout or a premium cement-based grout formulated for outdoor use. Confirm tile grout floor system is suitable for the specific indoor or outdoor application before grouting.
How water-resistant is epoxy grout compared to standard cementitious grout?

Epoxy grout is almost waterproof and is generally more water and chemical resistant than standard cementitious grouts. Epoxy resin tile grout offers high resistance to water, staining and chemicals, making it suitable for wet areas and demanding applications. Cementitious grouts, including sanded grout, are available in different formulations for interior and exterior use. However, epoxy grout does not eliminate the requirement for proper waterproofing.

Waterproof grout describes products with enhanced resistance, but the complete waterproofing system must still be correct. Select epoxy resin tile grout or cementitious grouts according to the tile, joint width, exposure and required water resistance, and confirm the system suits the installation.
What surface preparation is required before grouting tiled surfaces?

Before grouting tiled surfaces, the tile adhesive must be dry and set. Joints must be free from dust and debris. Highly porous tiles should be pre-dampened with water to prevent rapid moisture loss. A tile and grout cleaner can remove contaminants where necessary, but joints must be clean before applying grout for tiles. Use suitable tools for grouting to work grout fully into the joints.

When grouting floor tiles, confirm the selected grout suits the joint width, tile type and location. Sika Australia offers cement-based and epoxy-based grouts for different applications. Confirm the substrate and joints are ready before grouting floor tiles and proceed according to the product data sheet.
Is tile grout suitable for swimming pools and other submerged areas?

Yes, tile grout is suitable for swimming pools and other submerged areas, but premium high-performance products are recommended because pool water chemistry can be aggressive towards grout. Premium cement-based grouts are suitable, with epoxy tile grout being the best solution for grout for swimming pools and swimming pool grout applications.

Waterproof grout and epoxy tile grout should be selected according to the tile, joint width and pool conditions. For submerged areas, confirm the grout is specified for continuous water exposure and that the complete tiling and waterproofing system is suitable. Select grout for swimming pools carefully and follow the product data sheet for mixing and application.
Why does tile grout crack, discolour or fail over time?

Tile grout can crack if the substrate is not rigid enough or if there is a lack of expansion joints in the tiling system. Cementitious grouts are subject to discolouration over time, so premium higher-performance cement-based grouts can be considered, or high-performance stain and chemical resistant epoxy grouts. Efflorescence on tile grout can cause a white grout appearance.
For grout repair, products such as Davco Rejuvenation Grout

can be used as part of a suitable repair solution. White grout discolouration and efflorescence on tile grout should be assessed, and the grout system selected for the exposure and movement conditions. Confirm the grout suits the expected service and cleaning regime.
How much grout coverage is needed and how do I estimate quantity for a tiling job?
Grout coverage depends on tile size, tile thickness and joint width. To prepare a grout estimate, use the Sika grout calculator
or the coverage table for the selected product with the specific tile format and joint width. A grout calculator helps confirm how much grout is needed before grouting and sealing.
For tile grout how to guidance, confirm coverage before starting and allow extra for wastage. SikaCeram-690 Elite

is a high-performance cementitious tile grout for joints from 1 mm to 10 mm, suitable for porcelain, glass, ceramic and discolouration-sensitive natural stone, indoors, outdoors and in pools. The product data sheet gives the most accurate figure for the grout estimate.

By definition, waterproofing is the formation of an impervious barrier which is designed to prevent water entering or escaping from various sections of building structures. Areas where moisture can pool, such as bathrooms, laundries and external wet areas, must be waterproofed before tiling to contain moisture and protect the building structure.

Our waterproofing membranes offer a variety of features and benefits and are designed for commercial and residential applications. Depending on the area to be waterproofed, our range includes ready-to-use acrylic and polyurethane membranes that can be applied directly out of the pail. We also have cementitious 2 part membranes that eliminate the need for reinforcement layers, thus saving application time and mess.

Waterproofing membranes are suitable for internal wet areas such as shower recesses, toilets and laundries, external wet areas such as roofs, decks and balconies and other applications such as planter boxes, water tanks, ponds retaining walls, swimming pools and spas.

A waterproofing bond breaker is designed to allow normal building movement to be accommodated by a waterproofing membrane. Bond breakers allow the membrane to stretch, rather than snap, taking advantage of the elastic property of the material.

What is waterproofing and why does it matter for Australian buildings?

Waterproofing is a product or coating that prevent the passage of water or vapour from passing or migrate through building materials or elements. It is important to prevent water and vapour ingress from entering building elements and causing water damage.

Left unprotected, water can cause damp, mould, damaged finishes and corrosion of reinforcement, leading to costly repairs. Cement waterproofing is one option within the wider range of technologies, and floor waterproofing is a key part of protecting wet areas. Sika Australia provides waterproofing mortars, flexible and liquid-applied membranes, injection grouts, coatings and joint sealants, selected to suit the project requirements.
Which type of waterproofing membrane is best for a roof?

There is no single waterproofing membrane that is best for every roof. The appropriate system depends on the roof design, service conditions and project requirements. Sika Australia provides several waterproofing technologies, including flexible membrane systems, liquid-applied membranes, coatings and sheet membrane systems.

For concrete roof waterproofing membrane applications, the substrate and required waterproofing performance should guide system selection. A flat roof waterproofing membrane also needs to suit the roof's drainage requirements, while a self adhesive waterproof membrane sheeting system may be considered where a sheet membrane technology is appropriate. Sika Australia recommends selecting the membrane system to suit the specific service criteria and project details.
How long to wait for concrete to cure before waterproofing?

The required curing time before applying waterproofing to a waterproofing concrete slab depends on the specific membrane system and substrate conditions. For a foundation waterproofing membrane, the substrate must be sufficiently dry and prepared according to the product data sheet. Substrate preparation is critical to achieving a successful bond, and membrane application must achieve the recommended dry film thickness.

Different Sika Australia waterproofing products have varying moisture tolerances. As a general guideline, allow the concrete to cure and dry sufficiently before applying waterproofing. Ideally, the concrete’s relative humidity should be below 75% before application. If the reading is higher, application may still be possible with certain systems, provided the moisture conditions are assessed.
Can waterproofing products be used to repair leaking roofs?

Yes, waterproofing products can be used as part of the repair of roofs, provided the selected system is suitable for the roof substrate, service conditions and the specific source of water ingress. Sika Australia offers several waterproofing technologies, including flexible membrane systems, liquid-applied membranes, coatings and spray-applied membranes.

For leaking structures, Sika Australia also provides injection systems designed for waterproofing buildings and underground structures. Sprayable waterproofing is one available technology, but the appropriate system should be selected according to the project requirements. Proper substrate preparation and membrane application, including the recommended dry film thickness, are important considerations for successful waterproofing.
What's the best practice to waterproof a shower or wet area?

Best practice for waterproofing a shower or wet area begins with selecting a suitable waterproofing membrane. Ensure substrates are fixed according to the manufacturer and designed to receive tiles. Prime surfaces with a suitable primer compatible with the substrate and selected membrane. Apply a minimum of two coats of the selected waterproofing membrane, allowing drying between coats. Inspect each coating after application for defects.

Allow drying in accordance with the PDS before subsequent coverings. Waterproofing mortars can be used beneath tiling systems to help prevent water infiltration. Ensure compliant falls manage surface and subsurface water, and use a shower water sealer where specific wet-area requirements and standards apply.
Is Sika waterproofing suitable for commercial buildings like hospitals?

Yes, Sika Australia waterproofing systems can protect commercial building applications from water ingress. The range covers basements, underground structures, bathrooms, kitchens, balconies and water-retaining structures, with flexible membranes, liquid-applied membranes, waterproofing mortars, injection grouts and coatings.

For a hospital flooring, select the waterproofing system for the specific service criteria, exposure and building project details. Hospital flooring often uses vinyl, so the membrane should be coated with a suitable skim coat before vinyl flooring fixing.
What sealants are used alongside a waterproofing membrane?

Sealants used alongside a waterproofing membrane depend on the joints, interfaces and substrate details within the system. Sika Australia includes joint sealants as part of its broader waterproofing technologies, alongside flexible and liquid-applied membranes, waterproofing mortars and coatings.

Products such as sika self leveling sealant or an external door sealant may be relevant to specific joint or perimeter applications, but their suitability depends on the substrate and membrane system. Tooling caulking and a plastic adhesion promoter should only be specified where the relevant product documentation supports their use. Compatibility with the complete waterproofing system must be confirmed before application.
What's the difference between polyurethane and cementitious waterproofing coatings?

Polyurethane water proofing and cementitious coatings are different waterproofing technologies, and the appropriate choice depends on the substrate, service conditions and project requirements. Sika Australia offers flexible membrane systems, liquid-applied membranes, waterproofing mortars and coatings for different applications.

An elastic polyurethane coating typically provides flexibility and crack-bridging properties, while cementitious coatings are rigid and suitable for different substrate conditions. A pu floor sealer may form part of a floor waterproofing system. Product-specific technical documentation should confirm suitability, as performance differences depend on the formulation rather than the general category alone.
How are construction joints waterproofed to prevent water ingress?

Construction joint waterproofing typically uses a suitable joint treatment system designed to contain water and prevent water ingress through the joint. Sika Australia identifies the installation of a waterstop angle as an important consideration for containing water in wet areas and lists construction and movement joints among its waterproofing system applications.

The appropriate solution depends on the joint design, substrate and service conditions. Sika Australia’s waterproofing technologies include joint sealants, waterproofing mortars, flexible and liquid-applied membranes, injection grouts and coatings. A sika waterproofing compound should only be selected where its product documentation confirms suitability for the specific construction joint application.

The lifespan of waterproofing depends on the system, service conditions, substrate and quality of installation. Best practice focuses on selecting a membrane system that suits the service criteria, with proper substrate preparation and application of the recommended dry film thickness.

The time takes for waterproofing to remain effective can therefore vary between projects. Appropriate system selection, correct installation and attention to project-specific details are important for achieving long-lasting, watertight structures. Sika Australia does not provide a single service-life timeframe, as performance depends on exposure conditions and maintenance.

What are injection waterproofing systems and how do they stop water ingress?

Injection waterproofing systems seal water-bearing cracks, joints or construction interfaces by introducing a suitable resin or grout into the affected area. During concrete injection, the material travels through cracks or designated injection points and forms a barrier that helps prevent further water ingress.
Sika Australia offers several systems for different requirements, including Sika Injection-306

. Hydrophilic products such as SikaFuko systems and SikaSwell profiles use water-reactive technology for sealing construction joints. The appropriate system depends on the joint, leak condition and required waterproofing approach.
Which injection system is suitable for sealing water ingress through concrete cracks?
The suitable system for concrete crack injection depends on the crack and the required waterproofing approach. Sika Australia provides polyurethane injection options including Sika Injection-111
, a hydrophobic semi-flexible polyurethane injection grout, and Sika Injection-222
For permanent watertight sealing, Sika Injection-306

is a polyacrylic elastic injection resin suitable for crack and joint injection and sealing water-bearing cracks. Crack injection should be selected according to the specific water ingress and concrete conditions. Sika Australia offers a range of injection systems, and the appropriate choice depends on whether the priority is waterproofing or structural repair. Epoxy injection is also available for rigid structural bonding applications.
How is a polyurethane resin injected into a concrete crack to stop water leakage?

Polyurethane injection involves introducing a suitable polyurethane grout into a concrete crack through an injection system to address water leakage. For polyurethane resin injection, Sika Australia provides Sika Injection-111
, a hydrophobic semi-flexible polyurethane injection grout that reacts with water to create a hydrophobic foam and stop active water flow.

is a hydrophilic flexible polyurethane grout that reacts with water to form a permanently flexible seal. A leak injection system should be selected and installed according to the relevant Sika Australia technical information. Injection pressure, equipment and port spacing are specified in the product data sheets and should be followed for successful sealing. Sika Australia provides detailed application guidance for its injection systems.
Can injection waterproofing be used for basement and below-ground structures?

Yes, injection waterproofing can be used for basement and below-ground concrete structures where water ingress needs to be addressed. Sika Australia provides injection products and systems for sealing construction joints and water-bearing areas, including Sika Injection-306

These systems can form part of a basement waterproofing strategy, particularly where injection is appropriate for the specific leak or joint condition. The supplied Sika Australia information does not specify a basement waterproofing membrane, negative side waterproofing method or detailed foundation injection procedure, so these applications should be selected according to the relevant project requirements and Sika Australia technical documentation.
Are hydrophilic waterstops suitable for construction joints in concrete structures?
Yes. Hydrophilic waterstops are suitable for sealing construction joints in concrete structures, particularly non-movement joints. SikaSwell A profiles and SikaSwell S-2
hydrophilic sealant swell when they come into contact with water, helping seal construction joints and concrete penetrations.
For a waterstop for concrete walls, the appropriate system depends on the joint and project requirements. SikaSwell P Profiles

are also designed for construction joints, including precast concrete applications. These products form part of Sika Australia's range of construction joint waterstop solutions for watertight concrete systems.
How effective is polyurethane injection at sealing structural cracks under water pressure?

Polyurethane injection can be effective for sealing leaking concrete cracks exposed to hydrostatic pressure, provided the appropriate polyurethane system is selected for the conditions. Sika Injection-111 is a hydrophobic polyurethane grout designed to stop active water flow and water ingress, including leaks in concrete cracks and joints.

is a hydrophilic polyurethane grout that reacts with water to form a permanently flexible seal and is suitable for hydrostatic pressure environments. Polyurethane crack injection should be selected according to the crack condition and required performance, with structural crack repair assessed separately where load transfer is required.
What substrate conditions are needed before carrying out crack injection works?

Before crack injection, the concrete should be assessed to confirm that the crack and surrounding substrate are suitable for the selected injection system. For concrete crack repair, the substrate condition, crack characteristics and presence of water influence the injection approach and material selection.

Sika Australia’s crack injection guidance recommends drilling and installing mechanical packers capable of withstanding the required injection pressure, with slow, low-pressure injection generally preferred to rapid, high-pressure injection. For concrete injection repair, the appropriate equipment and resin also depend on whether the objective is waterproofing or load transfer.
Can crack injection systems be used to repair cracks in foundations and retaining walls?

Yes, crack injection systems can be used for foundation crack injection and some retaining wall cracks, mainly where controlling water ingress is the goal. Sika Australia provides polyurethane and polyacrylic injection resins for sealing cracks and joints, including Sika Injection-306 for water-bearing cracks.

For concrete foundation crack repair or concrete wall crack repair, assess the crack first: flexible polyurethane systems are typically used for waterproofing, while concrete crack injection epoxy provides rigid structural bonding. If cracks are structural or still moving, have an engineer assess the cause before repair.
Why does water continue to leak through a crack after an initial repair attempt?

Water can continue leaking after an initial repair if the selected injection system does not match the crack and water conditions, or if the crack has not been completely sealed. Sika Australia notes that long-term watertightness depends on selecting the appropriate injection material for the specific leak.

For example, leaking cracks under hydrostatic pressure may require a staged injection approach using a temporary waterstopping material followed by a flexible resin for permanent sealing. Basement leak repair, concrete slab crack repair and epoxy injection crack repair therefore require assessment of the crack, moisture conditions and repair objective before treatment.
What is the difference between epoxy injection and polyurethane injection for crack repair?

Epoxy and polyurethane injection are used for different crack repair requirements. Epoxy injection generally provides rigid bonding and is used where structural bonding or force transfer across a suitable crack is required. Polyurethane injection is more commonly selected for waterproofing leaking cracks, as certain Sika Australia polyurethane injection materials are flexible and can react with water to form a seal.

The choice depends on whether the priority is structural crack repair or stopping water ingress, along with crack condition, movement and hydrostatic pressure. For leaking cracks, pu injection and urethane injection systems can provide suitable flexible, water-reactive sealing when specified correctly.

What are the benefits of BIM?
When Building Information Modeling is used to its greatest potential, it can optimize the entire process of building, from early preliminary design through to construction and operations.

The MacLeamy curve shown was developed by Patrick MacLeamy, chairman of HOK (global architectural design and services firm), to represent the advantages of replacing a traditional drafting-centric workflow with a BIM workflow. The investment during the detailed design phase in the BIM workflow allows for a greater ability to impact cost and performance, which results in a reduction of overall costs. By focusing efforts earlier on in the design phase, the BIM workflow can save a lot of time, effort and resources later on.
Benefits of working with BIM include the following:

The project team can find discrepancies between various disciplines earlier in the project and avoid reworking later on when costs and time needed increase. For example, if a structural beam conflicts with a mechanical duct, it could be noticed within the BIM model and resolved prior to construction.
Better collaboration, reduced errors, and fewer requests for information and

confusion on the construction site are a few of the ways BIM brings about more productive workflows. The dynamic features of BIM software allow for faster design changes and embedded data in the model shared with the entire project team saves communication time.

Along with increased productivity, comes savings in labor and material costs on a project, from the design phase through to construction. Because design and construction are dynamically linked in the BIM workflow, time needed to execute design changes, and produce construction documentation is reduced significantly.

According to the McGraw-Hill Construction report, over 80% of expert BIM users report positive returns. After initial investment and BIM workflow integration, most project teams notice reduced design change costs, less time needed to manage requests for information during construction and ultimately an optimized profit-earning potential.

BIM is becoming more commonly requested by clients, owners and governmental agencies. Therefore, to be able to offer superior services to your clients, you have to maintain a competitive edge. Your clients will be happy to hear how they too can save time and money by working with you.

Detailed data about every aspect of the building is factored into the BIM model. Therefore, it is a true digital representation of the building, which can be provided to the building owner for easier long term operation, maintenance and repairs.

Building Information Modelling is essentially the evolution of the Construction Industry. Industry has been evolving for years, with new innovation, machines and automated production. Now the Construction industry needs to catch up.
BIM is not owned by anyone. It is not CAD or a single piece of software. BIM is a process, a new way of working which requires various tools, applications and a combination of software packages.

The ultimate goals are to increase the quality and performance buildings, improve communication / collaboration between all parties throughout the building lifecycle, reduce costs, reduce the potential risks/liabilities for all involved with the use of pre-site simulations and clash detection.

"BIM is essentially value creating collaboration through the entire lifecycle of an asset, underpinned by the creation, collation and exchange of shared 3D models and intelligent, structured data attached to them."

All stakeholders are involved and work together on one 3D building model, which ensures coordinated planning with less failures and better managed interfaces. As an intelligent 3D model-based process, BIM equips architecture, engineering, and construction professionals with the insight and tools to more efficiently plan, design, construct, and manage buildings and infrastructure.
"BIM is described in many ways, but at heart it is a collaborative way of working, supported by software tools that make information about buildings available and analysable"

The tools behind BIM are digital and require trained professionals who understand the workflow and chosen software platform. With the right tools, BIM brings your entire project to your team’s fingertips for faster coordination in the office and on the construction site, whether on a computer, tablet or smartphone device.

BIM adds a new dimension to the design process and requires a new way of thinking beyond traditional two-dimensional pen and paper methods. The entire project team will succeed when they embrace the third dimension and additional data, such as material properties, quantities, manufacturer-specific product details and more, which is embedded into the BIM workflow.

BIM is not a software, but a process to design, collaborate, simulate, check and control the design and building processes in a virtual environment. The activities around BIM are independently driven, since it doesn’t belong to any company, association or country. BIM is developing on a global level, and also has some local, country specific factors.

Water leaks and waterproofing issues are common in ensuite bathrooms. Regardless if the property is a new build or an older style home, leaks can cause stress for owners as they can be costly if left untreated.
Here’s what to do if your ensuite has waterproofing issues that result in a leak.
Waterproofing: the first line of defence
When waterproofing in a bathroom or ensuite fails it can be disastrous and can result in expensive renovations including removal of walls and extensive structural damage.
There are specific waterproofing requirements for bathrooms to ensure the process is done correctly.
