Sikafloor HB-22 PurCem: 9mm Heavy Poly/Cement system
Jointing Solution: Sikaflex Tank high-wear and chemical-resistant polyurethane sealant

Replacement of failed joint sealant (unknown type) in a weir leading to a potable water channel. The area will experience intermittent fast moving & rapid water flow over the top of the joint when in use during peak periods of high-water demand. The original joint sealant was applied during construction in dry conditions however as the asset is now in service the joint repairs were required for both above and below the water level. For protection of the substructure, it was necessary to waterproof all joints.
The area shown below will have live water flow across the weir from the reservoir into the water channel when in use.

Sika was specified by the consulting engineer, Arup, in this instance the solution was selected with technical support and guidance from the Sika specification team. The design solution for these emergency repairs included a full Sika system for joint repairs above and below the water line.

Joint waterproofing solutions were required for application above the water line and below the water line. All joints were up to 40 mm width, all existing sealants were to be completely removed. Due to the high abrasion conditions during water flow the engineer proposed to cover the joint repairs with a steel cover plate.

Due to different conditions a separate solution was required for below and above the water line. Above the water line a detail design including a high-performance joint sealant and waterproofing tape was proposed. Below the water line an injection system was selected due to the requirement to displace water out of the joint and allow placement of a joint waterproofing solution.

Above the water line application: Removal of existing failed sealant from unknown source. Preparation and cleaning of the joint surface and application of Sikaflex PRO-3 Purform. The Sikaflex PRO-3 Purform joint will be later covered with Combiflex SG system, EPDM rubber and mechanically fixed steel cover plate. Underwater joints will be treated separately with Sika injection systems.

Below the water line application: this joint was required to be waterproof to prevent water ingress to the below substructure and it was necessary to apply the solution while the joint was fully immersed under the water. A cover plate was applied to allow the injection application of Sika Injection-111 directly into the joint, the expanding urethane foam filled the joint and displaced the water. A second injection layer using Sika Injection-306 acrylate resin provided the final seal of all voids to form a waterproof joint.
Following the discovery of large cracks in the concrete slabs a dual use commercial and retail complex in Chatswood was deemed to have structural strengthening issues in the multilevel carpark.
An Engineering report was completed and recommended significant structural strengthening was required to 2 levels in the carpark.
The carpark slabs were to be strengthened around the pillars using a unique combination of Carbon fibre laminate and Carbon Rods.
Once completed the repairs needed to be able to withstand high volume heavy vehicle traffic from both the residential tenants and commercial customers.
The Sika Carbodur rods were laid in the direction of the steel across the slabs whilst the Sikacarbodur S1012 Laminate was laid above the rods
An Epoxy repair product Sikadur 31/41 was laid over the top of the repairs and to protect the Sikacarbodur and was sand seeded to an ant slip and abrasive resistant surface for the vehicle traffic
In Collaroy, a unit complex faced concrete spalling issues, leading to waterproofing problems impacting the balconies and some internal units. The cause of the extensive damage was magnesite.
A Consulting Engineering report was completed, with recommendation to significant repairs for most of the balconies and some units affected by concrete spalling caused by magnesite.
Following on from the spalling repairs all the units and balconies required waterproofing to ensure the minimisation and prevention of future issues.
was specified as the concrete repair mortar.
was specified as the corrosion inhibitor for the steel reinforcement and as a primer for the 412NFG.
Moisture Seal 2k was used as the primer and Sikatite Undertile as the waterproofing membrane.

The establishment of the Sydney Cricket Ground dates from 1854 and since then, it has been into a sacred site of Australian sport. a venue revered by sporting stars and spectators alike, the SCG is easily recognisable by its heritage listed members and ladies pavilions.

The heritage listed members stand incorporates an earlier three storey stuccoed brick club room at the rear As well as Lady Members Stand which is an elegant two-level grandstand constructed of cast iron and with an extensive three storey members' room at the rear.

The existing coating on the heritage listed Ladies and members stands failed in many spots resulting in water leakage to the heritage structure. Years of partial repairs and patching with various materials declined the integrity of the floor coating allowing water reach to the stand’s structure and the lower spaces. In addition, using inadequate material and application process resulted in slippery or very coarse, hard to clean patches all over the floor.

Replacing the existing floor coating in both Ladies and members stand with a durable, trafficable waterproofing membrane to withstand tremendous movements of the building during the matches and to meet the strictest Australian standards for the safe, non-slip floors

Sika proposed fully removal of the existing floor coating from all raisers and landings, removal of all sealant in the joints, Prep and sand the surface followed by applying Sikafloor 160 broadcasted with 30/60 quarts sand, then applying 3x coats of Sikafloor 400N.
For the non-slip, 8% of white Aluminium Oxide was mixed into the final coat of Sikafloor 400N to achieve P5 anti-slip rate.
Sikafloor 400 N was thickened by Sikadur 513 for the vertical application on the stand raisers.
Corner joints were sealed using Sikaflex Fillet and trafficable joints by Sikaflex TANK

Sika also proposed to carry out a 20 m2 test sample on the Ladies stand to asses the substrate conditions,moisture content of the substrate and to conduct a Pull of test and slip testfor documentation purpose.

When the 700m² showroom floor of the John Hughes Volkswagen dealership at Victoria Park, Perth was to be retiled, Davco’s Ultrabond primer/bond enhancer was selected to prepare the surface for tiling.

According to David Mortimer Operations Manager of City Tile Contractors, the preferred contractors for the project, when the old carpet was ripped up a surface contaminated with old adhesive was exposed.

“We consulted Davco and it was decided that Ultrabond was the best product to use for this project. Without Ultrabond it would have been necessary to machine sand to remove the old adhesive or scabble the concrete. These methods are often unsatisfactory and are very time consuming, not to mention very expensive.”

“Ultrabond was the ideal product because it allowed tiling to be carried out straight over the old contaminated surface. There was no sanding required and that meant no dust spreading throughout the premises, which was operational throughout the refurbishment period.”

“It was a much cleaner process and a lot less expensive. Importantly for the dealership it was also a much faster job enabling the tiling to be done quickly and efficiently to allow the new cars to go back on show in the refurbished showroom.”

Ultrabond’s quick curing time, 6-8 hours at 20ºC, is another important benefit in critical projects such as a major new car showroom. The surface can be quickly tiled over using any of Davco’s cement based or 2 part adhesives. It will also enhance the bond of tile adhesives onto substrates.
The fact that Ultrabond was chosen for this prestigious car showroom is recognition that Davco has the right products to complete cost-effective projects backed by superior technical support.
